name: Quanzhou Jinjiang International Airport
before:
Quanzhou's airport, 12 km south of the city centre in Jinjiang, and a joint military and commercial field, so parts of the site are not public.

It handled 8,852,384 passengers in 2025, almost exactly level with the year before.

The airport opened in December 1996 and was upgraded to international status in November 2012.
after:
Quanzhou's airport, 12 km south of the city centre in Jinjiang, first built as a military airfield in 1955.

It handled 8,852,384 passengers in 2025, almost exactly level with the year before.

The airport was upgraded to international status in November 2012.

claims.claim: joint military and commercial field; parts of the site not public
claims.wasBefore: and a joint military and commercial field, so parts of the site are not public
claims.why: Today's joint use rests on Wikipedia, with only a name in OurAirports ('Jinjiang Air Base') beside it; CAOP gives the military origin (1955) but says nothing of today's use, and nothing says which parts are closed. Softened to the 1955 military origin, which two sources give.

claims.wasBefore: The airport opened in December 1996 and
claims.why: Wikipedia alone (civil operations from 12 December 1996). The operator's site (qzair.com), which Wikipedia cites, timed out to a plain fetch and answered 502 in the browser; CAOP gives 1955 and 2012 but not 1996. With the 1955 military start now stated, 'opened in 1996' would also mislead without 'to civil flights'.

claims.claim: flights abroad, including a new Cebu route for summer 2026
claims.note: Fujian News Broadcast (29 March 2026), crediting the airport among its sources: the summer 2026 season plans 1,719 movements a week and adds Cebu, Nanchang, Linyi and Weihai. CAOP (undated) says it has international, regional and domestic routes. The Manila Bulletin's report of Fujian to Cebu flights (February 2026) sits behind a Cloudflare check and was left alone.
